title: Minimal Hedge Hypergraphs and Identification Reliability in Probabilistic Mixed Graphs
banked_reason: The proposal headlined a general-b accepted-output-delay compiler, but the proved theorem delivers only raw-Steiner-candidate-sensitive total time and leaves that delay object open.
gap_reasons: The proposal headlined a general-b 2^{O(b log b)}-preprocessing, accepted-output-delay compiler, but this theorem delivers only raw-Steiner-candidate-sensitive total time and leaves that delay object open; retitle/reposition the result around the weaker compiler (or prove the promised recursion).
The framing accurately distinguishes these proved results from the unresolved general-b delay claim, so there is no stale overclaim.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the sparse-core reduction, an exact candidate-sensitive general-width compiler, the complete district-width-two polynomial-delay construction, the width-two counting reduction, and post-compilation reliability/derivative evaluation. The promised general-width accepted-output-delay result collapsed at the cross-core domination problem: avoiding previously found obstructions couples a hypergraph-transversal constraint to multiple-root reachability, and bounded district width supplies no extension oracle. The canonical finite partial-support state, child partition, and nonempty-completion test therefore remain open and cannot be replaced by the proved raw-candidate-sensitive bound.
tldr: A probabilistic ADMG currently yields one high-plausibility identifiable realization, not the total chance that a fixed causal query is identifiable or the minimal edge combinations that destroy it.  The project makes those combinations the hyperedges of \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) and compresses every hedge into a \(2b-2\)-edge core plus directed ancestry obligations.  For general \(b\), the proved exact compiler projects deterministic reachability, enumerates raw minimal directed-Steiner witnesses, tests global minimality across every core, and suppresses duplicates canonically; its \(2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n)(1+W)\) total-time guarantee is explicitly sensitive to the number \(W\) of raw witnesses and is not an accepted-output delay bound.  The enumeration headline is the complete \(b\le2\) labelled transition-DAG and induced-path algorithm with polynomial preprocessing, worst-case delay, exhaustion, and space.  Once \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) is explicit, standard exact literal-weighted CNF model counting on a supplied incidence decomposition yields reliability and all edge sensitivities, while exact successful-realization counting is \(\#\mathrm P\)-complete already at \(b=2\).
gap: Ordinary ID certifies failure in one ADMG by a hedge, and edgeID chooses one plausible identifiable subgraph, but neither theory enumerates the globally minimal uncertain-edge causes of failure across all realizations.
fill: The project supplies a sparse-core representation, a canonical duplicate-free compiler with a complete width-two construction, a standard weighted-model-counting implementation corollary for the compiled output, and a sharp width-two causal counting-complexity boundary.
